research_question: What is the effect of interleukin-1 receptor antagonists (anakinra and canakinumab), compared with placebo or usual care, on all-cause mortality for secondary prevention in people with established cardiovascular disease?
positive_direction: Positive values favor the interleukin-1 antagonist group (indicating lower all-cause mortality / reduced risk of death compared to control)
search_queries: interleukin 1 antagonist cardiovascular disease mortality randomized trial
anakinra canakinumab myocardial infarction death controlled trial
IL-1 receptor antagonist secondary prevention all-cause mortality trial
inclusion_criteria: Empirical comparative studies (e.g., randomized controlled trials or controlled clinical trials) evaluating interleukin-1 receptor antagonists (anakinra or canakinumab) versus placebo or usual care
Adult participants with established cardiovascular disease undergoing secondary prevention (e.g., acute myocardial infarction, stable coronary artery disease, heart failure)
Reporting of quantitative data on all-cause mortality at follow-up
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, conference abstracts without data, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between an interleukin-1 antagonist treatment group and a control group (placebo or usual care)
No quantitative outcome data allowing calculation of an effect size for all-cause mortality (event counts, hazard ratios, odds ratios, or relative risks)
Studies conducted in populations without established cardiovascular disease or evaluating non-IL-1-targeted therapies
moderators_to_extract: Clinical condition / patient population (e.g., acute coronary syndrome, stable CAD, heart failure)
Study design and risk of bias
